tasks.title: Window waiters requeue onto the wrong channel
tasks.initial_signal: A desktop app can miss a deferred close event after an empty poll and then block forever even though input delivery still works for another window.
tasks.public_signal: One GUI handoff path hangs only after an empty first wait.

mutations.invariant: A waiter that sees no ready event must requeue onto the same keyed wait structure it was popped from.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden GUI cases park waiters on multiple window ids, force an empty first read, and then verify that only the matching window wake drains the requeued slot.

mutations.invariant: The SDK wrapper must preserve the caller-selected window key when it forwards the blocking event ABI.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: The hidden desktop suite waits on two windows concurrently and catches cross-window wakeups that public single-window smoke coverage misses.

tasks.title: Snapshot retention tracks the newest reader instead of the oldest
tasks.initial_signal: Recovery occasionally replays metadata that should still be hidden behind an older live snapshot when a newer reader is also active.
tasks.public_signal: A reboot path exposes too-recent metadata under concurrent readers.

mutations.invariant: Checkpoint reclamation must be pinned by the oldest active snapshot, not the newest one.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden WAL tests overlap an old reader with a newer one, then checkpoint and recover; the wrong comparison silently passes simpler single-reader cases.

mutations.invariant: The host-side recovery oracle must compute the highest dirty dependency across the flushed range.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private oracle-comparison runs force mixed dirty LSNs in one page range and catch a mirrored host/kernel drift that normal public page writes do not isolate.

tasks.title: Directory rename loses descendant protection and reverses paths
tasks.initial_signal: A rename that targets a nested destination can create a subtree cycle or move the wrong pathname when the source and destination are both valid.
tasks.public_signal: Ordinary file renames work, but one deep directory move poisons later lookups.

mutations.invariant: Rename must reject moving a directory into itself or any descendant to preserve an acyclic parent chain.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden namespace tests build multi-level directory chains and verify parent traversal after reboot, which exposes a false-safe ancestor check.

mutations.invariant: The user SDK must preserve source and destination ordering for atomic rename.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden CLI and GUI rename flows invoke the SDK wrapper rather than raw syscalls and catch a reversal that public low-level coverage can miss.

tasks.title: Scheduler accepts runnable slots without a live context
tasks.initial_signal: A resumed process can be chosen by the ready queue even when its context slot was never restored, leading to a late handoff trap.
tasks.public_signal: Scheduler epoch advances, but one resumed child traps immediately.

mutations.invariant: A runnable process cannot be scheduled until it owns a valid saved context pointer.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden handoff cases create runnable-but-uninitialized slots through interrupted launch paths and catch a scheduler that only checks state bits.

mutations.invariant: Public scheduler tests must still assert a real context-switch progression signal, not just queue activity.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: The private suite relies on the public test staying strict enough to reveal epoch progress regressions before deeper VM handoff checks run.

tasks.title: Required-LSN tracking becomes non-monotonic under buffer pressure
tasks.initial_signal: Large writes remain readable, but an older buffered page image can become flush-eligible again after a later update.
tasks.public_signal: Persistence drifts only after multiple writes to the same inode.

mutations.invariant: Per-inode required durability metadata must only move forward as newer writes commit.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden multi-write cases force an inode through repeated partial writes and reclaim; the inversion is invisible when each inode is written once.

mutations.invariant: Public regression coverage must reject unchanged dependency metadata after growth, not only decreasing values.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private stress runs depend on public checks preserving a strict monotonicity oracle before they add cache-eviction interleavings.

tasks.title: Base-27 grouped formatting drifts away from canonical 0z27
tasks.initial_signal: The guest SDK and host symbolic helpers still round-trip digits, but one grouped spelling no longer matches the canonical prefix contract.
tasks.public_signal: A symbolic dump looks almost right except for its prefix.

mutations.invariant: The guest formatter must emit the exact canonical grouped prefix accepted by the rest of the stack.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden guest parity tests compare exact byte-for-byte symbolic text, not just parsed numeric equality.

mutations.invariant: Host tooling and guest formatting must share the same stable textual contract for base-27 dumps.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private diagnostics tests diff host and guest symbolic artifacts directly and catch a prefix drift even when both sides still parse their own output.

tasks.title: Uppercase exact-trit literals stop classifying as numeric
tasks.initial_signal: Lowercase 0t literals still work, but one uppercase exact-trit spelling falls back into the non-numeric path in part of the stack.
tasks.public_signal: One assembler literal works in lowercase only.

mutations.invariant: Guest numeric parsing must treat uppercase and lowercase exact-trit prefixes consistently.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden guest probes feed both public and compatibility spellings through the same parser and reject case-sensitive drift.

mutations.before:
return token.size() >= i + 2 && token[i] == '0' &&
           (token[i + 1] == 't' || token[i + 1] == 'T' ||
            token[i + 1] == 'y' || token[i + 1] == 'Y' ||
            token[i + 1] == 'z' || token[i + 1] == 'Z');
mutations.after:
return token.size() >= i + 2 && token[i] == '0' &&
           (token[i + 1] == 't' || token[i + 1] == 'Y' ||
            token[i + 1] == 'y' || token[i + 1] == 'Y' ||
            token[i + 1] == 'z' || token[i + 1] == 'Z');
mutations.invariant: Host numeric-literal classification must preserve the exact accepted exact-trit prefix set.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private assembler and tool-path tests route tokens through both classification and full parsing, so a one-character whitelist drift becomes visible.

tasks.title: Host and guest disagree on the checked integer boundary
tasks.initial_signal: A boundary value is accepted by one numeric surface and rejected by another even though both claim the same exact T40 contract.
tasks.public_signal: Only one maximum-magnitude number fails to round-trip.

mutations.invariant: Guest symbolic conversions must expose the same checked integer range everywhere they promise exact T40 behavior.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden parity tests target only the cliff-edge values near the published maximum, where most public random cases never land.

mutations.invariant: The host parser must admit the maximum representable magnitude while still rejecting true overflow.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private tool tests exercise exact-limit decimal and hexadecimal spellings and compare them against guest SDK acceptance.

tasks.title: Rename lowers as reboot in the runtime wrapper table
tasks.initial_signal: A wrapper name is accepted by the compiler, but the emitted service id no longer matches the VFS rename ABI.
tasks.public_signal: One wrapper compiles and then calls the wrong service.

mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden corpus cases invoke rename from app code and validate both syscall number and side effects, catching a drift that public compile-only checks can miss.

tasks.title: wait_event lowers as direct window polling
tasks.initial_signal: Blocking event waits compile, but the lowered code uses the immediate poll syscall instead of the blocking wait service.
tasks.public_signal: The wrapper returns quickly but never blocks.

mutations.invariant: Blocking wrappers and direct polling services must remain distinct lowering targets even when they share argument shapes.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private window tests require a blocked status on empty queues and therefore catch a mistaken direct-read lowering immediately.

mutations.invariant: The public SDK must preserve the blocking wait contract rather than silently substituting a best-effort poll.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden integration cases call the SDK directly from apps and assert blocked-state behavior before any event arrives.

tasks.title: app_spawn reverts to the legacy static spawn path
tasks.initial_signal: A three-argument app launch compiles, but the lowered service and SDK argument order no longer match the live process ABI.
tasks.public_signal: New app launches return a result, but the wrong slot or pid is wired through.

mutations.invariant: The compiler must target the current process-launch ABI rather than a legacy service with different semantics.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden launch tests validate child slot, pid, and namespace propagation, which diverge immediately when the legacy service is used.

mutations.invariant: The SDK must preserve the published child-slot then child-pid ordering for app_spawn.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private handoff tests launch more than one child and confirm both pid bookkeeping and MMU window mappings, exposing a swapped tuple.

tasks.title: Assembler grouped literals use the wrong alphabet on the zero branch
tasks.initial_signal: Grouped symbolic numeric literals still parse for one family, but a base-27 token can be decoded with the base-81 alphabet in a narrow path.
tasks.public_signal: One grouped literal form miscompares in assembler parity checks.

mutations.invariant: Base-27 and base-81 grouped literals must retain distinct digit alphabets across every branch of the parser.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden assembler parity cases mix both grouped literal families in the same source and compare against the host symbolic implementation.

mutations.invariant: Public parity tests must continue to exercise the base-27 literal family instead of accidentally collapsing coverage onto base-81.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private symbolic-assembler tests intentionally keep both families live; weakening the public fixture leaves the parser bug visible there.

tasks.title: yield aliases to sleep_ms instead of sleep

tasks.public_signal: Yielding code suddenly behaves like a timed wait.

mutations.invariant: The published alias table must keep zero-argument yield mapped to the legacy cooperative sleep service.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden wrapper suites compile both aliases and compare emitted service ids against the manifest alias contract.

mutations.invariant: Name-to-service lowering must preserve the zero-arg wrapper ABI instead of selecting a same-family service with different arity and blocking semantics.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private compiler cases call yield inside tight loops and catch the semantic shift when it starts routing through the timed blocking path.

mutations.invariant: The guest SDK's zero-argument sleep wrapper must keep lowering directly to the canonical cooperative sleep service.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden guest-wrapper checks compile SDK callers through the Trit surface and compare the emitted service ids against the alias contract, so a wrapper that picks up a drifted alias is exposed.

tasks.title: getproc accepts short user spans and swaps its argument order
tasks.initial_signal: Process metadata can partially publish into user memory when a borderline pointer is accepted and the SDK forwards pid and output in the wrong order.
tasks.public_signal: One getproc caller corrupts a nearby sentinel instead of failing cleanly.

mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden pointer-fuzz cases probe exact-boundary spans where a zero result must still be treated as invalid, then verify that sentinels remain intact.

mutations.invariant: The SDK wrapper must preserve the pid then output-buffer ordering used by the syscall ABI.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private app-level process inspectors call the SDK rather than the raw syscall and catch the bad ordering together with the pointer-boundary mistake.

tasks.title: Process snapshots overrun their declared record window
tasks.initial_signal: The process snapshot syscall can accept a count that no longer matches its documented five-word user record shape, and the wrapper forwards the two arguments backwards.
tasks.public_signal: ps works for small counts but a larger request scribbles past the user buffer.

mutations.invariant: The count limit must be derived from the documented five-word record width and the fixed user window size.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden pointer tests request near-limit snapshots sized exactly to the documented window and detect the widened acceptance range by sentinel damage.

mutations.invariant: The public ps wrapper must preserve pointer then count ordering for snapshot writes.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private guest smoke apps call os_ps through the SDK and expose both the oversized count path and the argument inversion.

tasks.title: wait_event accepts a zero-span buffer and the SDK writes one word late
tasks.initial_signal: Window event waits can appear to succeed while shifting their event payload one word past the caller buffer.
tasks.public_signal: A blocked event call corrupts the word after the destination buffer.

mutations.invariant: wait_event must reject a destination span that is exactly out of bounds rather than publishing a partial event record.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden pointer fuzz uses precise end-of-page buffers and sentinel checks to catch a zero-span acceptance hole.

mutations.invariant: The SDK must write event records into the exact caller-provided base address.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private GUI tests validate the full four-word event record at the supplied address and catch the one-word shift immediately.

tasks.title: sleep_ms stops fast-returning on zero timeout
tasks.initial_signal: A zero-millisecond sleep can block instead of yielding a completed result, and the public wrapper routes the call through the untimed sleep alias.
tasks.public_signal: sleep_ms(0) no longer returns immediately.

mutations.invariant: A non-positive sleep_ms timeout must complete immediately without queueing state.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden scheduler tests interleave zero-time sleeps with futex wakes and catch a process that was incorrectly blocked.

mutations.invariant: The timed sleep wrapper must not collapse onto the legacy untimed sleep alias.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private guest tests compare zero, positive, and negative timeout behavior through the SDK and catch the alias substitution.

tasks.title: Window close requests wake the wrong state path
tasks.initial_signal: A close request appears to succeed but behaves like a present call in user code, leaving blocked window waiters stranded.
tasks.public_signal: Closing a window bumps presentation state instead of delivering a close event.

mutations.invariant: The close-request syscall must enqueue close-state transitions, not route through the framebuffer-present path.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private GUI cases wait for cooperative close delivery and verify that presentation counters and close queues remain independent.

mutations.invariant: The public window-close wrapper must preserve the dedicated close-request ABI.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden app flows exercise only the SDK wrapper and catch the state-path substitution even when raw kernel tests still pass.

tasks.title: Killed children stop releasing their windows before parent wait
tasks.initial_signal: A killed child remains visible in the window table until the parent reaps it, even though other teardown state looks correct.
tasks.public_signal: A child dies, but one window sticks around until later.

mutations.invariant: Process teardown must release windows by live pid ownership, not by an internal slot identifier with a different namespace.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden kill-and-wait cases create multiple processes whose slot numbers differ from pids, exposing a stale window-owner release path.

mutations.before:
kernel.windowCount() == 0,
           "killed child releases files, memory, and windows while waiting for parent");
mutations.after:
kernel.windowCount() >= 0,
           "killed child releases files, memory, and windows while waiting for parent");
mutations.invariant: Public teardown coverage must continue asserting full window cleanup before parent reap, not merely a non-negative count.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: The private process suite preserves the strict zero-window expectation and catches the ownership bug immediately.

tasks.title: Window launch accounting stops advancing across repeated app starts
tasks.initial_signal: Repeated launches of the same trusted app preserve functional behavior but the launch-count state no longer increments correctly.
tasks.public_signal: The app still runs, but one launch metric is frozen.

mutations.invariant: Trusted app launch accounting must advance once per successful launch so later state inspection reflects real scheduling history.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden repeated-launch cases verify monotonically increasing app metadata across desktop relaunches rather than just first-run success.

mutations.invariant: Public launch/handoff tests must continue requiring a clean halt, not merely avoid one specific failure status.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: The private suite still checks exact completion and associated launch metadata, so a frozen counter remains visible there.

tasks.title: reboot drifts to service 59 in the compiler-facing ABI

tasks.public_signal: reboot and rename appear to share a service id.

mutations.invariant: The compiler runtime ids must remain one-to-one with the published syscall table.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private wrapper and dispatch tests compare the tail services against both VM constants and live kernel behavior, exposing the collision.

mutations.invariant: The manifest must describe the same reboot id that compiler, VM, kernel, and SDK all export.

mutations.invariant: The guest reboot wrapper must continue invoking the reboot service exported by the manifest and compiler tables.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden guest ABI probes compile and inspect os_reboot callers without actually powering off the VM, so a wrapper collision with rename still gets caught.

tasks.public_signal: Empty waits stop looking blocked.

mutations.invariant: The calling-convention contract must continue documenting the same blocked code used by the live kernel.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden ABI validators compare live traces against the manifest and reject a matching but wrong success code.

tasks.public_signal: getproc returns the right data with the wrong register contract.

mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Private syscall-trace checks validate register placement in addition to user-buffer contents, so the misplaced length is visible.

mutations.invariant: The manifest's calling convention must preserve the stable payload/detail register split.
mutations.hidden_test_rationale: Hidden ABI checks compare manifest fields against captured syscall traces and reject any swapped register documentation.
